tasks.short: Pick workshops that fit the school's development plan, request leave and budget, attend meetings, conferences and workshops, log the hours and share what was learned.

steps.what: Special education teacher picks workshops that fit the school's development plan
Special education teacher e-mails the team leader for leave and budget
Team leader approves leave and budget
Special education teacher checks the enrolment before it goes: course, dates and cost as the team leader approved
Special education teacher registers for the workshop with the provider
Special education teacher attends professional meetings, educational conferences and teacher training workshops
Special education teacher logs training hours in a personal overview
Special education teacher shares what was learned in a team meeting

tasks.design: The school's training catalogue in the HR system ({HCM}) lists courses that fit the development plan with remaining budget, and leave and budget are requested there in one form for the team leader to approve. Once approved, the teacher checks the enrolment and sends it once to the provider and those providers report attendance into the teacher's training hours; for other courses the teacher uploads the certificate. Attending and sharing stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Courses were found by searching, requests sent by e-mail and hours kept in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: HR systems hold training catalogues, requests and attendance records.
tasks.still_hard: Finding cover for the class is the real obstacle to attending.
tasks.human_edge: Bringing back one idea the whole team can use on Monday.

reach.learn: Whether one form speeds up approvals.

evidence.claim: HR systems hold training catalogues, leave requests and attendance records.
Staff councils must consent to tools that can monitor staff.

assumptions: Boundary: from the development plan to shared learning; arranging cover is outside.
Input contract: catalogue kept by the HR adviser; attendance from catalogue providers; certificates from other providers; fallback is e-mail and spreadsheet.
Attending and sharing do not change.
Team leaders' time is outside the teacher's savings.
research_questions: Do teachers use more of their training budget?

incremental.description: No new ongoing work; checking reported hours is part of s6.

approvals.approved_version: The enrolment for the course, dates and cost exactly as approved by the team leader in s3 and checked by the teacher in s4b, sent once to the course provider; another course or cost needs a new approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most courses are outside the catalogue and need certificates uploaded, so s1 keeps 80 and s6 keeps 70 (12.0); high: most courses from the catalogue (19.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the agenda and papers, attend staff meetings and committee sessions, take the committee minutes, circulate them and follow up actions.

steps.what: Special education teacher reads the agenda and papers before the meeting
Special education teacher attends staff meetings and serves on committees
Special education teacher takes handwritten notes of the discussion: in every meeting today, only where a member does not consent to recording after the change
Special education teacher takes the committee minutes

loop.input: The meeting record (a recording made with every member's consent) and the agenda.
loop.output: Draft minutes with decisions and actions per agenda item.
loop.check: The teacher checks every decision and action against the meeting; the chair approves the minutes before they go out.
loop.stop: One draft per meeting; without consent there is no recording and the teacher writes the minutes.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning a discussion into decisions and actions needs free text.

steps.what: Committee chair approves the minutes
Special education teacher checks the minutes before they go out: it is the version the chair approved, to the committee members
Special education teacher circulates the checked minutes to committee members: by e-mail today, shared from the document space after the change
Special education teacher files the meeting notes after the minutes are approved
Special education teacher follows up the committee's actions

tasks.design: Agenda items link to their papers in the school's document space ({DOCS}). With every member's consent the meeting is recorded, and a bounded step drafts committee minutes with decisions and actions per item; the teacher checks them and the chair approves. The teacher checks that the approved version is the one shared and shares it once with members from the same space, and the recording is deleted on approval. Attending and following up stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Papers came in separate e-mails and minutes were typed from notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Meeting tools record and draft minutes; document spaces link papers to agendas.
tasks.still_hard: Members may not consent to recording; then minutes are written by hand.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a quiet colleague's view heard in the committee.

reach.learn: Whether drafted minutes free secretarial time.

evidence.claim: Meeting tools can record meetings and draft minutes with decisions and actions.
Staff councils must consent to tools that can monitor staff, such as meeting recordings.

assumptions: Boundary: from the agenda to followed-up actions; decisions themselves are outside.
Input contract: agenda and papers from the committee chair; consent from all members; fallback is notes.
Attending and following up do not change.
The recording is deleted when the chair approves the minutes; without consent the teacher keeps notes.
The chair's approval time is outside the teacher's savings.

About 80% of meetings are recorded with every member's consent; in the rest the teacher still takes and files notes, so s3 and s7 keep 20. Circulating keeps 50 of s6; the check before it keeps its full time.

already_counted.description: Special education teacher checks the drafted minutes.

incremental.description: Special education teacher asks members for consent to record.

approvals.approved_version: The minutes exactly as approved by the committee chair in s5 and checked by the teacher in s6b against that version, shared once with the committee members from the document space; any change needs a new approval and check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a member refuses recording at about half the meetings, so notes stay by hand (s3 and s7 at 50) and minutes keep 75 (11.4); high: about 80% of meetings recorded and drafts need light edits (17.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the trip or project and book transport and venues, collect parent consent and medical details, do the risk check, supervise students during the activity and guide them in reflecting.

steps.what: Special education teacher plans field trips and class projects
Special education teacher looks up transport and venues and their prices
Team leader approves the trip plan and costs
Special education teacher checks the booking before it goes: supplier, date, times, numbers and cost as the team leader approved
Special education teacher books transport and venues with the supplier
Special education teacher prepares the consent and medical details request in the parent app
Special education teacher checks the consent request before it goes: date, place, programme and medical questions
Special education teacher sends the checked consent request to the parents in the parent app
Parents give consent and medical details: on a paper form today, in the parent app after the change
Special education teacher collects parent consent and medical details: paper forms today, from the app's list with reminders to parents who do not use it after the change
Special education teacher writes the risk check for the activity
Special education teacher supervises class projects, trips and guest speaker visits
Special education teacher guides students in learning from those activities

tasks.design: Transport and venues the school has used before are listed with contacts and prices in the school's document space ({DOCS}), so the teacher looks them up instead of phoning around. The team leader approves plan and costs; the teacher checks the booking and sends it once. The teacher checks the consent request and sends it once in the parent app ({OTHER}); parents give consent and medical details there, so fewer paper forms are chased. A risk check template starts from the last check for the same venue. Supervising students and guiding reflection stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bookings were phoned, consent forms collected on paper and risk checks written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Parent apps take digital consent and details.
tasks.still_hard: Some parents do not use the app; paper forms remain for them.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a student is overwhelmed by the crowd and stepping aside with them.

reach.learn: Whether a shared supplier list cuts booking time.

evidence.claim: Parent apps take digital consent and medical details for school trips.
Medical details of pupils are health data; keep only what the trip needs and delete afterwards.

assumptions: Boundary: from the activity idea to reflection; paying suppliers is outside.
Input contract: consent from parents in the parent app; supplier list kept by the school administrator; fallback is paper and phone.
Planning, supervising and guiding do not change.

Parents' time is shown in s5 at share 1 and priced as customer time; the team leader's time is outside the teacher's savings. s7 keeps 70 because the risk check is still judged for this group and day; the template saves rewriting the standard parts.
research_questions: Are all consents in before the day?

incremental.description: No new ongoing work; chasing parents is part of s6 and parents' entry is shown in s5.

approvals.approved_version: The booking with supplier, date, times, numbers and cost exactly as approved by the team leader in s3 and checked by the teacher in s4b, sent once to the named supplier; another supplier or a higher cost needs a new approval.

The consent request with date, place, programme and medical questions exactly as checked by the teacher in s5b, sent once to the parents of the students on the trip in the parent app; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half the parents stay on paper and venues are new each time, so s2 keeps 80 and s6 keeps 70 (9.2); high: most parents use the app and venues repeat (15.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare practical assignments in the vocational area, demonstrate and instruct in the workshop, record skills shown and prepare students for an internship certificate.

steps.what: Special education teacher prepares practical assignments in vocational areas
Special education teacher provides additional instruction in the workshop
Special education teacher notes which vocational skills each student has shown: on paper today, ticked per skill on a tablet after the change
Special education teacher photographs the student's work as evidence, framing the work and not faces
Special education teacher copies the skills notes into each student's portfolio
Special education teacher prepares students for an internship certificate

tasks.design: A bank of practical assignments per vocational area in the learning platform ({LMS}) gives a starting point that the teacher adapts. Skills shown are ticked on a tablet per skill with a photo as evidence, which takes about as long as paper notes but fills the portfolio for the internship certificate, so nothing is copied. Instruction and preparing students stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assignments were made per class and skills noted on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning platforms hold assignment banks and photo-based skill records.
tasks.still_hard: Workshop work is hands-on; records are a small part.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a student's pride when a piece of work turns out right.

reach.learn: Whether photo portfolios help placement talks.

evidence.claim: Learning platforms hold assignment banks and photo-based skill records.
Photos of pupils need consent under the school's pupil-data rules, agreed with the parents' and pupils' council.

assumptions: Boundary: from vocational goals to prepared students; placements are outside.
Input contract: assignment bank kept by the vocational department; fallback is paper.
Instruction and preparation do not change.
Photos show work, not faces, where possible.

Ticking skills is a first record and keeps its full time; the photo is shown as its own step (s3a). The photo goes only into the student's own portfolio in the learning platform, an ordinary save; only copying notes into the portfolio (s4) goes.

incremental.description: No new ongoing work; photographing work is shown as s3a.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the assignment bank has few items for this area and portfolios still need some copying, so s1 keeps 85 and s4 keeps 60 (5.7); high: the bank covers most assignments and portfolios fill from the tablet (15.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The special education teacher keeps training, meetings, trips and workshop teaching; requests, minutes, paper forms and paper skill lists shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher whose admin around trips and committees no longer eats into evenings.
